newsitem.title: USA: New York deepens NYNEX, Frontier resale discounts.
newsitem.headline: New York deepens NYNEX, Frontier resale discounts.

text.p: The New York Public Services Commission on Tuesday set permanent discounts that NYNEX Corp and Frontier Corp's Rochester Telephone Corp must offer rivals who want to use their networks to reach customers.

The discounts are dramatically deeper than temporary discounts set in July. NYNEX must now offer resellers a 21.7 percent discount from the retail rate on both business and residential lines if the reseller provides its own operator service and 19.1 percent if NYNEX provides operator service.
The temporary rates were 11 percent for business and 17 percent on residential lines, regardless of operator service.
For Frontier, discounts are broadened to 19.6 percent without operator service or 17 percent with. The interim discount was 13.5 percent for business and residential lines.
Frontier controls four percent of the state's telephone lines and NYNEX has 91 percent.
"The Commission's goal is to provide technically and economically viable opportunities for rapid and broad entry of competition (into local calling)..." the commission said.
Ironically, the discounts are in the middle of the 17-25 percent range that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) set as part of its interpretation of the 1996 Telecom Act.
The regional Bells and some states fought hard to challenge the FCC's jurisdiction to set rates, and the range of discounts which the Bells said was too deep.
They succeeded in winning a stay, or suspension, of the FCC pricing rules in October, but have found that states have been implementing similar discounts anyway.
Analyst Bette Massick of brokers Bear Stearns said that states such as New York which set their interim rates early were generally deepening the discount substantially.
"It is probably reasonable, so NYNEX is unlikely to be surprised," she said.
First arguments in the FCC case are due to be heard before the U.S. Appeals Court in St. Louis, Missouri in January. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1610
